chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a large village, and in it are 'uluj' (tax collectors/officials) from whom the Sultan takes fifty dirhams, and from some of them thirty, and less and more. What do you say if the Sultan makes a peace treaty (or agreement) with them, meaning the owner of the village, for something, and he takes from them more than what he gives to the Sultan? He said, he said: 'This is haram (forbidden).'

key_terms.حَرَامٌ: Forbidden or unlawful in Islamic law
key_terms.صَالَحَ: To make a treaty, agreement, or settlement
key_terms.عُلُوجٌ: Tax collectors or officials who collect taxes

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a tax collector taking more from the people than what he pays to the ruler?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares it *haram* for a village owner or tax collector to retain more from the populace than what is paid to the Sultan, even if an agreement exists. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of preventing *ghabn* (unfair exploitation) in public revenue collection, ensuring that intermediaries do not profit excessively at the expense of the common people.
